## Problem
Playtest anomaly (broken_link, high, system gear/tools): Gear prompts never trigger, so no tool can be obtained
Expected: Triggering Grab Axe, Grab Extinguisher or Grab Hose gives the player the tool, so they can fight fires, break doors and refill water.
Observed: Round 1: the judge reported high severity that the gear prompts never trigger. The counters have no extinguish, water, rescue or door activity at all, so the whole core loop was blocked.

## Root cause (from experiments in the running game)
Not conclusively proven. The gear prompts (InvPrompt on GearRack and Truck Locker parts) are built correctly: Enabled, Style Custom, HoldDuration 0, MaxActivationDistance 9, RequiresLineOfSight false, on anchored parts tagged GearRack. A fresh Custom-style control prompt placed next to one fired both PromptShown and Triggered, so the client prompt pipeline works. The gear prompt itself never showed or fired in any client probe, and the player's InvHand attribute stayed empty. The probes were partly confounded. Probe 3 waited only 0.5s after teleporting, and in probes 4 and 6 my control prompts were closer to the player than the gear prompt, so Exclusivity OnePerButton on the E key would hide the farther one. The most likely game-side defect is in how InventoryService hooks InvPrompt.Triggered and grants the item, because no gear was ever granted and the inv_grabs counter stayed at zero. Part of the failure may also be a test artefact, since a bot driving Custom-style prompts through InputHoldBegin may not reproduce what a real player does. I did not verify the server-side hook.
Evidence: Probe 1: the gear prompts exist and are enabled. Probe 5: no abnormal properties (Custom style, OnePerButton, Enabled true, HoldDuration 0). Probe 3: with no controls present, 3.4 studs away, the gear prompt's Triggered did not fire and InvHand stayed empty. Probe 4: a fresh Custom control prompt was shown and triggered (shown.b=true, res.b=true) while the gear prompt was not, but the controls were closer, so exclusivity may explain it. Probe 6: all gear prompts are enabled and within range, none was shown, and leftover control prompts were closer at 2.5 studs.
Fix hint: In InventoryService, check that every prompt tagged with the InvPrompt attribute is connected to a Triggered handler that calls Give(player, itemId) for GearRack and TruckCompartment parts. That includes racks built after startup, so hook them via CollectionService GetInstanceAddedSignal for GearRack and TruckCompartment as well as the initial sweep. Also make sure the handler does not return early when the player's hand is empty or the rack's Item attribute is missing, since the racks only carry a Slot attribute and must resolve through ItemDefs.RackOrder.

## Context
Game: Co-op chaotic firefighters on Roblox: alarm, burning town block, hose, axe, rescues, Blame awards.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Make every acceptance-critical object reachable and in range: keep doors, pickups and victims within tool range of walkable floor, and leave gaps wide enough for the character to pass.
- Lay out props so they never overlap or z-fight. Do not place coplanar surfaces (a pad on a road, a road on a road) at the same Y; offset them by at least 0.05 studs or use different thicknesses. Place buildings outside road footprints with a margin, and keep door pads on walkable ground. Place repeated props (houses, pads) on a deterministic grid or in lanes with explicit road exclusion zones and minimum spacing, not random ring angles. A ring of props around a hub collides with roads that cross the same area, so compute positions from the road layout. Also keep the spawn and key landmarks clear of each other and of the roads, and keep the spawn-to-first-objective distance short.
- Do not add decorative trim that sits inside another part's volume (for example a ring whose top is below the pad's top). It is invisible and wastes parts. Put trim above the surface or make it wider than the pad.
- Place collectibles (keys, coins, pickups) from a fixed, hand-vetted list of spots, one per room or zone, not random picks from a candidate pool. Each spot must be inside walkable floor, clear of walls and furniture, and away from the spawn. Random choice cannot guarantee reachability or spread.
- Keep spending, selling and other trigger pads out of walkable gameplay areas. Compute each pad's footprint from its real size, including its depth, and keep it clear of tile grids, paths and the spawn by a margin of at least a couple of studs. Ordinary walking or spawning must never trigger a purchase by accident. Derive positions from the grid's edges (edge of the nearest tile row, not its center), not from guessed offsets.
- Size platformer jumps conservatively for the default character. A jump clears about 7 studs of height and about 12 studs of distance. Keep the edge-to-edge gap to roughly 8 studs or less and each rise to about 4 studs or less. Measure the gap between edges, not centers, and leave margin for imperfect jumps. Make checkpoint and goal platforms at least as large as the others.
- Keep every tunable gameplay value (jump limits, speeds, catch distances, timers) in one source of truth (Config). Never add a second clamp, `math.max` floor or hard
